name: C11_H8_Z_FIBER_EXACT_QUOTIENT_THEOREM
fixed_context: One ordered type pair (T,T'), one stored 111 state (p,m,n), one post-Lemma10 descendant P'.
candidate_family: K_graph={(y,y',z): y in A, y' in B, yy' nonedge, z in Y0' cap N(y) cap N(y')}.
claims: The equivalence is graph/state-only and polynomially decidable.
Every equivalence class is exactly one nonempty z-fiber over an ordered pair (y,y').
Answer relevance is constant on each z-fiber.
The full {3,4}^2 extension projection on boundary coordinates (y,y') is identical for all class members.
A canonical summary is (T,T',p,m,n,y,y',z_can), where z_can is the least common witness under a fixed graph vertex order.
Summary size is independent of z-fiber multiplicity.
There are at most |A||B| <= n^2 classes.
The quotient and canonical certificates are polynomially discoverable without an extension oracle.
If a common witness lies in a connected component C of G[Y0'], descendant axiom (iv) forces y and y' complete to C, hence every vertex of C is a common witness.
nonclaims: No bound g(|S|) on survivor pairs.
No family-gate outcome selected because frozen precedence still audits F1 then F2 before F3.
